_comment: Hook wiring for harness-fitness.
Every command uses the portable interpreter idiom
`command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 X || python X`, because a bare
`python3` is absent on some Windows installs while a bare `python` is absent on
many Linux ones. A hook that cannot start is indistinguishable from a plugin
that does nothing — and for a measurement plugin that failure is silent twice
over: nothing breaks, and the numbers simply stay empty.
Timeouts are budgets, not expectations. `SessionStart` gets 15s for a job that
should take well under one, because it reads eight disk sources and a cold page
cache is not an error.
PreToolUse is deliberately absent, and so are SubagentStop, Notification and
PermissionRequest — see adr/004. abacus already owns the edit hot path with the
only hook whose response can stop a tool call; `tool_decision` and
`hook_execution_complete` already report every block, so a second blocking hook
there would buy nothing and cost latency on every edit. More generally, every
hook this plugin adds enlarges the composition it exists to measure, so the
instrument should be the smallest thing in the profile it prints (adr/006).
No hook here can influence whether a tool runs, and none emits
`additionalContext`. They all exit 0 and say nothing.
tests/unit/test_hooks_manifest.py asserts all of the above as data — the
manifest is the one artefact no other test exercises.
